Intel’s shares had climbed as high as 12% in Thursday’s after-market session just after the report. South Korea’s KOSPI declined 5.8% by Friday afternoon in Seoul, while Samsung and SK Hynix stocks slid 7.6% and 8.3%. The move in U.S. semiconductor stocks has become increasingly bundled with KOSPI, which is heavily weighted toward chipmakers Samsung and SK Hynix and has seen increased volatility lately. The Direxion Daily South Korea Bull 3X Shares (KORU), a three-times leveraged ETF tracking South Korea’s largest stocks, dropped 8.5%. The sentiment for the fund has dipped steadily over the past week and was ‘bearish’ as of the last reading. INTC was the top trending stock on Stocktwits early Friday, with retail sentiment moving to ‘extremely bullish’ from ‘neutral’ the previous day. Retail traders debated the company’s capital expenditure plans and foundry business update, while analysts noted that Wall Street had largely expected a strong quarter, with much of the optimism already priced into the stock ahead of the earnings release. “INTC no way intel will stay at 100 and plus with that higher capex announcement wall street gonna dump on us,” a trader wrote, while another said, “$INTC can't hold a 9% gain for a few minutes, we're stuck here until 2027.” Intel plans to spend $20 billion this year, up from its previous forecast of $18 billion, and could tap the capital markets for funds. Tech giants Alphabet and Amazon recently raised enormous amounts through debt and equity despite having significant cash already. “INTC says they won't ramp Capex unless they were confident in customer commitments. Since they're raising Capex "significantly" next year, that means they're confident in those 10 long-term customers,” Deepwater Management founder Gene Munster said in an X post. Based on Intel’s fine print, Munster broadly believes that the AI infrastructure buildout is still in its early stages, with demand for its CPUs benefiting from the broader hyperscaler investment cycle. While he sees Intel as a beneficiary of the AI boom, he believes Nvidia and AMD remain better ways to invest in the trend, noting that much of Intel’s recent optimism is already reflected in its valuation. Intel’s turnaround is closely tied to its foundry business, which recently bagged new marquee customers such as Apple and Tesla. The unit narrowed its operating loss to $2.1 billion from a $3.2 billion loss a year earlier, but did not announce new customer wins in the report. The government-backed chipmaker’s second-quarter revenue increased 25% to $16.1 billion and adjusted earnings per share came in at $0.42 per share. Wall Street analysts had anticipated $14.5 billion in revenue and an adjusted profit of $0.22 per share, as per Fiscal.ai. The revenue expansion was largely driven by Intel’s data center operations, where sales soared 59% last quarter to $6.3 billion. "In data centers, the CPU is taking off," CEO Lip-Bu Tan said in an interview with Bloomberg. "Demand is outpacing our increasing supply, and so those are good problems to have." Intel’s third-quarter sales and profit forecasts also came in above expectations. As of the last close, INTC shares had declined 29% from their peak on June 22 but remain 172% higher year to date. The company also generated $2.9 billion in free cash flow, supported by $3.2 billion in operating cash flow. This represented a strong rebound from the $150 million cash outflow reported in last year’s Q2. Lockheed Martin’s total backlog climbed to a record $230 billion, helped by major contracts such as expanded THAAD interceptor production and a $10.5 billion logistics agreement with U.S. Special Operations Command. “These awards are less about any single program than about what they were building in aggregate. Together, they strengthen the nation's production base, adding resilience along with more manufacturing capacity, more sources of supply and greater surge capability, all at a time when these very attributes have become a strategic imperative for the country,” said Lockheed’s CEO, James Taiclet, at the Q2 earnings call. title: Will Suncor's Refining Strength Continue to Drive Cash Flow? - The Globe and Mail
content: Suncor Energy Inc. SU continues to benefit from its integrated refining operations, supported by stronger refining margins, high utilization and growing refined product sales. The company's downstream business has become a significant contributor to cash generation, raising expectations about its ability to sustain profitability. In the third quarter of 2026, Suncor's Refining and Marketing segment generated C$3.61 billion in adjusted funds from operations, compared with C$1.22 billion a year earlier. Segment free funds flow increased to C$3.29 billion from C$926 million, reflecting favorable refining conditions. Higher cracking margins were a major contributor to the improvement. Operational performance remained encouraging, with refinery utilization reaching 95% and crude throughput of approximately 488,000 barrels per day. Refined product sales increased to a third-quarter record of nearly 677,000 barrels per day from approximately 647,000 barrels a year earlier. Previous debottlenecking initiatives expanded high-value export capacity, while stronger domestic retail sales supported performance. Suncor's integrated operations provide another advantage. The Edmonton refinery's direct connection to oil sands production improves feedstock flexibility and operational efficiency. This integration helped maintain refinery throughput during planned maintenance, while logistics capabilities largely offset supply disruptions in Eastern Canada. Looking ahead, Suncor's 511,000-barrel-per-day refining network, diverse crude sourcing and access to high-value markets support its cash generation potential. However, sustaining the recent momentum will depend on refining margins, product demand and continued operational reliability. ExxonMobil Holdings Corporation XOM also benefited from favorable refining conditions in the third quarter of 2026. The company's Energy Products earnings increased to $7.17 billion from $1.84 billion a year earlier. ExxonMobil achieved 100% crude unit utilization at the U.S. Gulf Coast refineries, reflecting strong operational performance and its ability to capture favorable margins. Chevron Corporation CVX reported downstream earnings of $4.93 billion, compared with $1.14 billion a year earlier, supported by higher refined product margins. The company's U.S. refineries achieved record crude throughput of 1.09 million barrels per day, with utilization approaching 98%. Chevron's reliable refining operations highlight its ability to benefit from favorable market conditions. Suncor's shares have gained 67.5% over the past year, outperforming ExxonMobil's 46.3% increase and Chevron's 39.7% rise. SU's stronger share-price performance reflects investor interest in its integrated operations, improved cash generation and shareholder returns. The gains also highlight growing confidence in the company's ability to sustain profitability across its upstream and downstream businesses. Suncor appears attractively valued compared with its integrated energy peers. The stock trades at a forward 12-month price-to-earnings (P/E) ratio of 9.59, below ExxonMobil’s 13.26 and Chevron’s 12.45. This suggests that investors can gain exposure to Suncor’s expected earnings at a lower price than those of its larger peers. The valuation discount, combined with solid refining operations and healthy cash generation, adds to the stock’s investment appeal. Over the past 60 days, the Zacks Consensus Estimate for Suncor's EPS has increased 18.54% for 2026 and 11.31% for 2027. The current estimates stand at $8.76 per share for 2026 and $7.28 for 2027. These upward revisions indicate improving analyst expectations for Suncor's earnings performance, supported by its integrated business model and favorable operating conditions. Suncor's strong refining performance, growing cash flow and integrated operations support its outlook. The stock’s attractive valuation relative to peers and upward earnings estimate revisions further strengthen its investment appeal, despite refining margin volatility.
